[Chunk 1]: D07 — Design Handoff & Accessibility | DeccanBridge Software 

 Design Handoff & Accessibility

  DeccanBridge Software — Synthetic Enterprise Policy D07  
 Version:  1.1 — Reconciliation candidate 
 Classification:  UI/UX / Standard (departmental) 
 Knowledge project:  UI/UX (organization-owned) 
 Policy custodian:  UI/UX representative (UI/UX employee; designated custodian) 
 Independent editorial reviewer:  Product Manager (Product Management representative) 
 Effective date:  1 November 2026 
 Scheduled review:  1 November 2027 
 Publication status:  Offline editorial candidate — not approved for publication, indexing, or employee retrieval

This document describes an internal B2B SaaS design-process scenario; it is not evidence of statutory accessibility compliance or a legally mandated design standard. Editorial acceptance does not grant access, release authority, expenditure authority or permission to publish the document.

 1. Purpose, audience and limits

 This procedure defines a traceable way to  prepare, review, hand off and validate user-interface designs and accessibility considerations  before Engineering implements them. It supports an employee's ability to ask the Knowledge Copilot who should provide design context, what evidence belongs in a handoff, how unresolved concerns are tracked and when a handoff does  not  constitute authorization to build or launch.

 D07 is a  UI/UX / Standard  departmental source. Active employees in the UI/UX home department are eligible to read its authorized published edition under current access rules. Employees outside UI/UX require an independently approved,  D07-specific Standard document grant valid for 90 elapsed days , subject to earlier revocation; this is not a company-wide permission. A Manager, CEO, COO or administrator gains no automatic right to read D07 through seniority or function. Participation in a design initiative also does  not  authorize viewing its linked files without each recipient's applicable permissions.

  Ownership distinction:  The UI/UX representative is D07's policy custodian. The Product Manager is its independent editorial reviewer, but must receive a separately approved,  D07-specific Standard reading grant valid for 90 elapsed days  before inspecting it; appointment as reviewer does not confer source access. Custodianship, design input, reading privileges, feature prioritization, Engineering sign-off and production-release authority are separate. Final design acceptance, accessibility acceptance and release-approval roles remain  unapproved .

 2. Working definitions and confirmed boundaries

 Term 
 Meaning in D07 
 Boundary 

 Design request 
 A request to investigate or change an experience 
 Not an approved Product feature or Jira issue 

 Design handoff 
 A permission-safe package of specifications, assets and open questions supplied for implementation review 
 Not a deployment, purchase or release approval

[Chunk 2]: Preserve access-scoped  design/business records  for requests, versions, permitted references, reviews, findings, handoff decisions, exceptions and revisions. Their definitive repository, schema, authorized readers and retention period are  not yet approved . Separately, authorized security-audit events form an  append-only, metadata-only stream retained for 365 days ; that stream must not store design/source passages, prompts, answers, screenshots or protected business record contents. The 365-day rule does  not  set the retention schedule for design/business records. Employee departure revokes individual privileges while company-owned policies remain subject to formally reassigned custodianship.

  Unresolved D07 business-policy decisions:  (1) accessibility standard/edition, conformance target and objective criteria; (2) supported devices, languages, browsers and assistive-technology matrix; (3) design-review, acceptance and final sign-off authorities; (4) design turnaround and defect remediation SLAs, if any; (5) canonical design/asset repository, version references and design-record retention; (6) accessibility exceptions or waiver authority, if any. Until separately approved, no numerical accessibility pass gate, turn-around target or authorization right may be inferred from this document.

  Related processes:  Employees may follow the company-wide Employee Handbook and  separately authorized  Product, Engineering, Project Management and cross-functional launch procedures. A cross-reference is not a permission grant, and the Copilot must not reveal the identity or contents of documents outside a requester's current access.

  End of D07 — Design Handoff & Accessibility. Synthetic Candidate 1.1 for offline editorial review only — NOT PUBLISHED.

[Chunk 3]: Accessibility review 
 Examination of likely barriers across supported interaction modes 
 Not a certification or claim of conformance to a particular standard 

 Acceptance criteria 
 Testable descriptions of intended user-visible behavior 
 The final approving role and mandatory template are unconfirmed 

 Handoff blocker 
 An unresolved dependency or material issue that requires decision 
 Not an automatically assigned numerical severity 

 Design change 
 A traceable update to a previously shared design 
 Does not silently supersede an approved product or engineering decision 

 Restricted evidence 
 Information requiring a document-specific grant 
 May not be copied into a broader design deliverable merely for convenience 

  Confirmed company context:  DeccanBridge is a fictional B2B SaaS organization. Its company-wide service window is  Monday–Friday, 9:30 AM–6:00 PM IST ; one operational business day is  8.5 service hours , with clocks paused outside service hours and on weekends. No separate holiday calendar is modeled.  D07 does not adopt a mandatory WCAG edition or conformance level, numerical contrast/pass threshold, accessibility sign-off role, design-handoff SLA or release gate.  The company calendar alone creates none of these obligations.

 3. Intake: establish the intended experience

 An authorized UI/UX contributor begins from a recorded, permission-safe request. The approved intake software, intake field schema and person empowered to accept design work are still open. The following is a  content checklist for an auditable record , not a finalized form or system requirement:

  Define the user problem.  Describe the persona or user group, the workflow, observed friction and desired outcome. Distinguish a verified observation from a hypothesis or stakeholder preference. 
  Establish the context.  Record the relevant screen or journey, supported platform assumptions, known states, integrations and dependencies. Do not assume which browsers, devices, languages or assistive technologies must be supported; these remain explicit product decisions. 
  Separate evidence from sensitive records.  Keep user research summaries, screenshots and analytics restricted to what each audience is permitted to see. Prefer synthetic examples over real customer credentials, private records or production data. 
  Link only permissible references.  A Product discussion, Engineering defect, project risk or launch activity may inform the work, but links and cited evidence must be authorized for each recipient. A reference cannot confer access. 
  Record unknowns.  Note unresolved user needs, edge cases, business decisions and reviewer assignments. An incomplete brief may be returned for clarification without being rejected or silently assumed complete. 

 Feature evaluation and prioritization belong to the separately authorized Product process. A design request or Product discussion cannot establish a Product score, automatically prioritize implementation, approve Engineering work or grant access to Product-only source material. Seek minimum-necessary, permission-safe direction from an eligible Product owner when a Product decision is required.

[Chunk 4]: Package the current version.  Supply authorized design references, intended behavior, known alternatives, accessible-interaction notes and unresolved items. Confirm the intended recipient can view each linked source. 
  Request appropriate review.  Seek UI/UX, eligible Product and Engineering input according to the work's scope. A reviewer receives only the minimum necessary material; a UI/UX Standard label does not make every design artifact company-wide. 
  Discuss implementation feasibility.  Verify whether the desired behavior is understood and identify technical, privacy, performance, accessibility and testing dependencies. Note where feasibility has not yet been assessed. 
  Record findings and ownership.  Distinguish an actionable design revision, a Product scope decision, an Engineering implementation question and a security/access request. Capture actual decisions and the authorized decision-maker when established. 
  Disposition unresolved concerns.  Mark them as needing clarification or valid authority rather than silently treating unanswered questions as accepted. Escalate material risk through the independently authorized route applicable to that work. 
  Communicate the handoff state.  Identify the version shared, items reviewed, unresolved blockers, actual recipients and next agreed step. Do not report “approved for development,” “accessibility passed” or “ready to release” when the respective authority or evidence is missing. 
  Handle change after handoff.  Record revised version, affected components, reason, potential rework and the eligible reviewers who need renewed input. Avoid issuing conflicting implementation instructions from an obsolete design link. 

  Acceptance and release are different gates.  Product priority, design readiness, code review, security approval and launch authorization remain separate decisions by eligible authorities. A design handoff does not establish a launch-approval deadline, approve a launch or grant access to project-shared source records. Coordinate through an approved, minimum-necessary handoff; the intended recipient must independently qualify to view each shared document or asset.

 Where a design proposal requires expenditure, independently designated Finance/budget authorities must approve applicable spending under their own rules. A design handoff, UI/UX sign-off, workaround or process exception cannot authorize spending or grant access to protected financial evidence.

 7. Accessibility findings, disagreements and exceptions

 A concern may be raised by a designer, engineer, tester, Product contributor or other eligible participant without granting them the right to inspect an inaccessible source. For disagreement, record the competing observed facts, design versions, test conditions, alternative approaches and what must be decided. If no approved severity scale or final acceptor exists, preserve that uncertainty; do not invent a blocking label or permit one party to self-certify compliance.

[Chunk 5]: Labels and semantics 
 Are controls and icons understandable by name and purpose? Is intended heading/landmark structure documented for implementation? 

 Text, graphics and contrast 
 Can users distinguish meaningful information? Are alternatives specified for informative non-text content, and is meaning not conveyed by color alone? 

 Forms and errors 
 Are required fields, validation errors, correction steps and status changes understandable and associated with the relevant input? 

 Responsive and zoom behavior 
 Do layouts and content remain usable in the supported viewport and text-scaling conditions, without losing critical controls? 

 Motion, timing and feedback 
 Are animations, time-sensitive interactions and status updates examined for user control, distraction and clarity? 

 Assistive technology and testing 
 Which actual combinations were tested, by whom, with what result? Which were not tested? 

  Recording practice:  For each relevant review topic, record the tested design version, environment, steps or scenario, observed result, supporting evidence, responsible follow-up and whether the observation is  verified ,  requires investigation  or  not evaluated . Do not convert “not tested” into “passes.” Do not fabricate contrast ratios, percentages, test coverage or a particular screen-reader result. If tests use real customer artifacts, access rules still apply to the evidence and resulting logs.

 When a proposed accessibility issue affects a production interface, distinguish a  design finding , an  Engineering bug , an  active incident  and a  future project risk . A relevant Engineering or Project Management owner must apply their separately authorized classification, triage and escalation procedures. D07 cannot assign their severity, start their service clocks or promise repair or resolution.

 6. Review, disposition and handoff to Engineering

 The following sequence is a  draft operational method consistent with approved governance . It does not establish yet-unapproved final sign-off roles, mandatory minimum reviewer counts or automatic merge/deployment gates.

[Chunk 6]: Allowed:  Answer a currently authorized employee's D07 question using the active accessible edition with a citation, clearly distinguishing confirmed operating rules from proposed review topics. 
  Missing evidence:  Say that a specific WCAG target, mandatory design turnaround, final sign-off role, browser matrix or pass threshold is  not approved in D07 . Do not invent it as company policy. 
  Denied access:  Do not expose restricted or inaccessible source titles, snippets, citation markers, metadata, design URLs or even confirming details about inaccessible documents. A generic permission-safe denial is appropriate. 
  Grant change:  When reading rights are revoked, protected D07 evidence must not appear in later answers, previews, citations or future Copilot context. Dependent earlier replies must be hidden from the affected requester as required by approved access governance. Material already delivered to a browser cannot be retroactively retracted. 
  Automated action:  A request to file a design bug is not by itself permission to create a Jira ticket. Where the separately authorized Engineering Jira/Activepieces action is available, the employee must first review a specific proposed draft, then give  explicit post-draft confirmation . The application must independently authorize the user, destination and safe payload and record the actual result. A D07 citation or design approval cannot bypass these checks; the SOP does not activate the integration. 

 A Product Manager serving as independent editorial reviewer must hold a separately approved,  D07-specific 90-elapsed-day Standard reading grant  that remains valid for review. The role alone grants no other UI/UX or departmental reading privilege. Design evidence and business records must be shared only with authorized recipients; their repository and retention schedule remain to be approved.

 9. Governance, audit and unresolved decisions

 The  UI/UX representative  approves D07 content and classification as custodian; the  Product Manager  independently reviews the wording only with a valid D07-specific Standard grant. After both approvals, the  Operations Knowledge Administrator  is the authorized final publisher for this Standard document. Publication and restoration are never implied by editorial review. A reclassification requires  quarantine during review ; withdrawn/superseded versions are excluded from active retrieval.  Emergency withdrawal  may be performed only by the authorized Security Administrator or a separately preappointed, narrowly scoped COO backup while its appointment is valid. Emergency authority does not confer reading, restoration or publication rights. Preserve protected provenance according to separate authorization.

[Chunk 7]: 4. Preparing an implementable handoff package

 The design contributor should supply a package precise enough for an eligible engineer or tester to distinguish intended behavior from gaps. Only material that the specific recipient may access belongs in the shared package; otherwise share a separately cleared summary and request appropriate access through normal governance.

 Handoff element 
 Content to record 
 Common uncertainty to flag 

 Scope and revision 
 Initiative reference, affected flow, design version, date, author or designated owner 
 Whether the referenced Product scope has been approved 

 Screens and flows 
 Main journey, navigation, empty/loading/error/success states, conditional transitions 
 Unsupported edge states or unclear user journeys 

 Interaction behavior 
 Inputs, actions, feedback, focus behavior and state changes 
 Undefined keyboard or assistive-technology behavior 

 Content and labels 
 User-facing copy, meaningful names, form help, validation and error wording 
 Localization, legal claims or customer-facing approval 

 Layout and assets 
 Responsive intent, typography, icons, image alternatives, export format and asset provenance 
 Device breakpoints, licenses or final engineering asset format 

 Accessibility evidence 
 Known barriers, review observations, test conditions, accepted limitations and remediation proposals 
 Chosen success criteria and reviewer authority 

 Handoff decisions 
 Questions, alternatives, dependencies, reviewers, rationale and disposition 
 Who may formally accept the handoff 

 Each design revision should have a distinguishable identifier or timestamp and a short change description; the exact version-numbering convention and system of record have not been approved. Do not silently replace a reference in a prior Engineering discussion: record what changed, why, which previously agreed behavior it affects, and who must review the change.

  Avoid a false completeness signal.  A clickable prototype may illustrate the happy path but fail to specify errors, permission-denied states, long content, responsive behavior or keyboard interaction. Mark such gaps explicitly. If a screen depicts personnel records, budgets, restricted policies or protected customer data, use appropriately sanitized or synthetic examples and apply the source's access controls rather than broadening distribution.

 5. Accessibility review: practical evidence, not unearned certification

 Accessibility is an important part of design quality, but  no binding WCAG edition or conformance level, test matrix, numerical contrast/pass criterion, formal sign-off role or accessibility waiver authority has been approved  for this fictional company. The following checks are  practical review topics, not certification criteria or mandatory release gates . Record observed evidence and gaps; an untested topic is not evidence of compliance.

 Review topic 
 Questions for the design and test record 

 Keyboard operation 
 Can expected actions be reached and operated without a pointer? Is focus order meaningful and visibly identifiable?

[Chunk 8]: Under the approved business-exception rule  BN1 , the  policy custodian or an expressly delegated authorized approver  may handle a D07 process exception  within their actual authority . The requester must not approve their own exception. Keep a trace of requester, reason, affected step, eligible independent approver, decision, constraints, expiry or review point if set, and follow-up. A process exception cannot override document access rules, separately required funding approvals, or valid release/security gates. There is  no approved blanket accessibility waiver authority , and this draft does not create one.

 For inaccessible evidence, decide separately (a) who may  read the source  and (b) who may  approve the related business action . A design custodian or reviewer does not acquire rights to other departments' protected policies, previews or attachments merely because those sources could help a decision.

 8. Publication, knowledge access and safe AI behavior

 D07 is an  organization-owned, UI/UX / Standard  policy. Employees may rely on it as a Copilot source only after UI/UX custodian content/classification approval, separately authorized independent Product editorial review, authorized publication by the Operations Knowledge Administrator and successful indexing.  Candidate 1.1 is offline, unpublished and not eligible for employee retrieval.  These editorial words do not grant repository, release, document or tool permissions.

 The Employee Knowledge Copilot may retrieve and cite only  currently authorized, published  evidence. Document access must be enforced by the application's authorization checks and underlying data controls  before protected source material is retrieved ; instructions supplied in a chat cannot create rights. A project selector may narrow permitted sources, never widen them. A response, preview, citation or source link must not disclose a document that the requester cannot currently read.

 A concern may be raised by a designer, engineer, tester, Product contributor or other eligible participant without granting them the right to inspect an inaccessible source. For disagreement, record the competing observed facts, design versions, test conditions, alternative approaches and what must be decided. If no approved severity scale or final acceptor exists, preserve that uncertainty; do not invent a blocking label or permit one party to self-certify compliance.

[Chunk 4]: Preserve access-scoped  design/business records  for requests, versions, permitted references, reviews, findings, handoff decisions, exceptions and revisions. Their definitive repository, schema, authorized readers and retention period are  not yet approved . Separately, authorized security-audit events form an  append-only, metadata-only stream retained for 365 days ; that stream must not store design/source passages, prompts, answers, screenshots or protected business record contents. The 365-day rule does  not  set the retention schedule for design/business records. Employee departure revokes individual privileges while company-owned policies remain subject to formally reassigned custodianship.

  Unresolved D07 business-policy decisions:  (1) accessibility standard/edition, conformance target and objective criteria; (2) supported devices, languages, browsers and assistive-technology matrix; (3) design-review, acceptance and final sign-off authorities; (4) design turnaround and defect remediation SLAs, if any; (5) canonical design/asset repository, version references and design-record retention; (6) accessibility exceptions or waiver authority, if any. Until separately approved, no numerical accessibility pass gate, turn-around target or authorization right may be inferred from this document.

  Related processes:  Employees may follow the company-wide Employee Handbook and  separately authorized  Product, Engineering, Project Management and cross-functional launch procedures. A cross-reference is not a permission grant, and the Copilot must not reveal the identity or contents of documents outside a requester's current access.

Dependent earlier replies must be hidden from the affected requester as required by approved access governance. Material already delivered to a browser cannot be retroactively retracted. 
  Automated action:  A request to file a design bug is not by itself permission to create a Jira ticket. Where the separately authorized Engineering Jira/Activepieces action is available, the employee must first review a specific proposed draft, then give  explicit post-draft confirmation . The application must independently authorize the user, destination and safe payload and record the actual result. A D07 citation or design approval cannot bypass these checks; the SOP does not activate the integration. 

 A Product Manager serving as independent editorial reviewer must hold a separately approved,  D07-specific 90-elapsed-day Standard reading grant  that remains valid for review. The role alone grants no other UI/UX or departmental reading privilege. Design evidence and business records must be shared only with authorized recipients; their repository and retention schedule remain to be approved.

 9. Governance, audit and unresolved decisions

 The  UI/UX representative  approves D07 content and classification as custodian; the  Product Manager  independently reviews the wording only with a valid D07-specific Standard grant. After both approvals, the  Operations Knowledge Administrator  is the authorized final publisher for this Standard document. Publication and restoration are never implied by editorial review. A reclassification requires  quarantine during review ; withdrawn/superseded versions are excluded from active retrieval.  Emergency withdrawal  may be performed only by the authorized Security Administrator or a separately preappointed, narrowly scoped COO backup while its appointment is valid. Emergency authority does not confer reading, restoration or publication rights. Preserve protected provenance according to separate authorization.

[Chunk 6]: Under the approved business-exception rule  BN1 , the  policy custodian or an expressly delegated authorized approver  may handle a D07 process exception  within their actual authority . The requester must not approve their own exception. Keep a trace of requester, reason, affected step, eligible independent approver, decision, constraints, expiry or review point if set, and follow-up. A process exception cannot override document access rules, separately required funding approvals, or valid release/security gates. There is  no approved blanket accessibility waiver authority , and this draft does not create one.

 For inaccessible evidence, decide separately (a) who may  read the source  and (b) who may  approve the related business action . A design custodian or reviewer does not acquire rights to other departments' protected policies, previews or attachments merely because those sources could help a decision.

 8. Publication, knowledge access and safe AI behavior

 D07 is an  organization-owned, UI/UX / Standard  policy. Employees may rely on it as a Copilot source only after UI/UX custodian content/classification approval, separately authorized independent Product editorial review, authorized publication by the Operations Knowledge Administrator and successful indexing.  Candidate 1.1 is offline, unpublished and not eligible for employee retrieval.  These editorial words do not grant repository, release, document or tool permissions.

 The Employee Knowledge Copilot may retrieve and cite only  currently authorized, published  evidence. Document access must be enforced by the application's authorization checks and underlying data controls  before protected source material is retrieved ; instructions supplied in a chat cannot create rights. A project selector may narrow permitted sources, never widen them. A response, preview, citation or source link must not disclose a document that the requester cannot currently read.

[Chunk 7]: Labels and semantics 
 Are controls and icons understandable by name and purpose? Is intended heading/landmark structure documented for implementation? 

 Text, graphics and contrast 
 Can users distinguish meaningful information? Are alternatives specified for informative non-text content, and is meaning not conveyed by color alone? 

 Forms and errors 
 Are required fields, validation errors, correction steps and status changes understandable and associated with the relevant input? 

 Responsive and zoom behavior 
 Do layouts and content remain usable in the supported viewport and text-scaling conditions, without losing critical controls? 

 Motion, timing and feedback 
 Are animations, time-sensitive interactions and status updates examined for user control, distraction and clarity? 

 Assistive technology and testing 
 Which actual combinations were tested, by whom, with what result? Which were not tested? 

  Recording practice:  For each relevant review topic, record the tested design version, environment, steps or scenario, observed result, supporting evidence, responsible follow-up and whether the observation is  verified ,  requires investigation  or  not evaluated . Do not convert “not tested” into “passes.” Do not fabricate contrast ratios, percentages, test coverage or a particular screen-reader result. If tests use real customer artifacts, access rules still apply to the evidence and resulting logs.

 When a proposed accessibility issue affects a production interface, distinguish a  design finding , an  Engineering bug , an  active incident  and a  future project risk . A relevant Engineering or Project Management owner must apply their separately authorized classification, triage and escalation procedures. D07 cannot assign their severity, start their service clocks or promise repair or resolution.

A clickable prototype may illustrate the happy path but fail to specify errors, permission-denied states, long content, responsive behavior or keyboard interaction. Mark such gaps explicitly.
